heldout.known_failures_rule: all mismatches on live_stack (both variants) and policy_only/context_bound; baseline and lockdown are comparison arms (see failed_case_ids).
limitations: Same-author fixtures: cases, registry, components and metric definitions were written by one author who knew the code under test. Expect optimistic results; this is not an independent red team.
Small N: 40 cases total, roughly half per split, a handful per label. Wilson 95% intervals are wide; escalation and several categories have single-digit denominators.
In-process latency only: perf_counter around adapter/gateway/approval calls on a shared dev host. No network, no model, not GB10, not end to end.
No model in the loop: proposals are scripted; nothing measures whether a real agent would produce them.

Circular authority oracle: the registry/authority record both decides and defines harm, so live-stack attack success is near 0 by construction wherever the record covers the attack. Not independent evidence.
Egress provenance tags (prov, labels) are hand-written by the fixture author; payment provenance is derived by the adapter from the same registry. Neither is runtime-supplied provenance.
Parser-failure and oversized-input cases are non-actions (DECISIONS 11); they are included in attack_success_rate but excluded from attack_success_rate_substantive, which is the headline.
Policy-only results include cases no policy could affect (schema failures, approver excluded); those cases dilute differences between policies.

Split is fixed by id hash before running; with N this small it does not guarantee balanced coverage and the dev/heldout distinction protects against tuning only because cases were never edited after running.
Approver cases use a fixed fake clock and a rehearsal-grade event shape; real Discord event authenticity is outside this suite.
